artworks.title: Aeneas Fleeing from Troy
artworks.description: Batoni's flight from Troy keeps Creusa in the family group — Priam's daughter and Aeneas' first wife still present as the city burns, before she vanishes in Virgil's dark streets.

artworks.title: Aeneas Fleeing Troy with Anchises, Creusa, and Ascanius
artworks.description: A Metropolitan Museum print after Aeneid 2 names Creusa among the fleeing household — wife, father, and son in the moment before she is lost.

artworks.title: Aeneas and the Ghost of His Wife Creusa
artworks.description: The Virgilian farewell: Creusa's shade appears to Aeneas after the sack — not to follow him west, but to free him for Italy and Lavinia.

films.title: The Trojan Horse
films.description: Ferroni's peplum keeps the Trojan household in the burning city — Creusa among the doomed generation Aeneas must leave behind.

popCulture.title: Aeneid
popCulture.creator: Virgil
popCulture.description: Virgil gives Creusa her ghost-speech in Book 2: the wife who cannot sail for Italy, blessing Aeneas' future kingdom as she fades into Troy's night.

popCulture.title: Creusa (wife of Aeneas)
popCulture.description: Daughter of Priam and Hecuba, first wife of Aeneas and mother of Ascanius — lost in the sack, remembered as a shade.
